<output>
Swiss Java Knife (SJK)
=========

SJK is a command line tool for JVM diagnostic, troubleshooting and profiling.

SJK exploits standard diagnostic interfaces of JVM (such as JMX, JVM attach and perf counters) and adds some more logic on top 
useful for common troubleshooting cases. SJK can also be used as a library for building application specific diagnostic tools
or to enhance your code with self monitoring features.

What you can do with SJK?
----

 - [Monitor Java threads in real time][ttop]
 - [Analyze head dynamics with advanced class histograms][hh]
 - [Access MBean attributes and operation from command line][mx]
 - Create [flame graphs][html-flame] and over reports from snapshots created VisualVM, Java Flight Recorder or [SJK's own sampler][stcap]
 
See [full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md).

Download
----

Latest prebuild binaries [![Last Version](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/org.gridkit.jvmtool/sjk.svg)](https://search.maven.org/#search%7Cga%7C1%7Cg%3A%22org.gridkit.jvmtool%22)
- `wget https://training.ragozin.info/sjk.jar` -> [sjk.jar](https://search.maven.org/remotecontent?filepath=org/gridkit/jvmtool/sjk-plus/0.22/sjk-plus-0.22.jar) 

Starting sjk
----

    java -jar sjk.jar <cmd> <arguments>
    java -jar sjk.jar --commands
    java -jar sjk.jar --help <cmd>

Below a few command from SJK ([full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md)).

[ttop]
----

Pools thread CPU usage of the target JVM and periodically reports to the console.

 - can attach via PID or open JMX port
 - displays thread memory allocation rate and cumulative process allocation rate
 - displays safe point time consumption (only if attache via PID)

[More details][ttop]

[hh]
----

Similar to `jmap -histo`.

 - plus can show a histogram of dead objects (histograms of all and live requested, then difference is calculated)
 - plus can show N top buckets in histogram

[More details][hh]

[stcap], [stcpy], [ssa] and [flame]
----

These commands provide basic sample profiler capabilities. `stcap` produces hyper-dense stack trace dump 
(about 1000 compression rate compared to text format) and `ssa` provides few reports over dump files.
`stcpy` can copy data in archives produced by `stcap` (e.g. merging dumps or filtering selected threads).

So far following reports are available:

 - [sophisticated filtering] (time, stack trace, thread name)
 - stack frame histogram with advanced filtering options
 - flame graph visualization (SVG or [interactive HTML][html-flame])
 - per thread summary (CPU usage, memory allocation, etc)
 - converting back to text format

Dump file can be also processed programatically.

[More details][ssa]

[mx]
-----

This command allows you to do basic operations with MBean from command line.

It can:

 - read MBean attributes
 - update MBean writeable attributes
 - invoke MBean operations (arguments are supported)
 - display composite and tabular data in a human readable format
 - use wild cards to shorten MBean names (e.g. `*:*,name=CodeCacheManager` instead of `java.lang:type=MemoryManager,name=CodeCacheManager`)
 - connect to local JVM processes by PID (e.i. any Java process, you do not need to enable JMX server)
 - connect to JMX using host:port (password authentication is supported)

[More details][mx]

[jps]
----

Similar to `jps` from JDK. 

- plus can display specific system properties of process in output
- plus can display values of specific -XX for HotSpot JVM processes 
- plus can filter process java processes by their system properties
 
</output>

{"command": "# The compiler process finishes quickly. Let's create a longer-running process.
# We'll run the compiler in a loop and also with JMX enabled
cd /workspace && cat > long_run_compiler.sh << 'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  java -Xmx512m -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=9010 -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=false -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.ssl=false -jar /workspace/closure-compiler.jar --compilation_level=ADVANCED --js=/workspace/sample.js --js_output_file=/workspace/output_long_${i}.js 2>/dev/null
done
SCRIPT
chmod +x long_run_compiler.sh

# Kill any existing background processes
pkill -f "closure-compiler.jar" 2>/dev/null
sleep 1

# Start the long-running compiler loop
nohup bash long_run_compiler.sh > /workspace/compiler_long.log 2>&1 &
echo "Background script PID: $!"
sleep 1

# Find the actual java process
java -jar /workspace/jvm-tools/sjk/target/sjk-0.24-SNAPSHOT.jar jps 2>&1"}

{"command": "# Let's create a comprehensive summary report
cat > /analysis-results/ANALYSIS_SUMMARY.md << 'SUMMARY'
# JVM-Tools (SJK) Analysis of Closure-Compiler

## Overview

This report documents the analysis of the **Google Closure Compiler** project using the **jvm-tools (SJK - Swiss Java Knife)** diagnostic tool.

## Tools Used

- **jvm-tools (SJK)**: Built from source at https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools
  - Version: 0.24-SNAPSHOT
  - Build command: `mvn clean install -DskipTests -DdisableToolchain`
  - JAR location: `/workspace/jvm-tools/sjk/target/sjk-0.24-SNAPSHOT.jar`

- **Closure Compiler**: Pre-built jar from Maven Central (v20260629)
  - Source code cloned from https://github.com/google/closure-compiler
  - 817 Java source files, 274,880 lines of code
  - 6,668 classes in the compiled JAR

## SJK Commands Executed

### 1. jps - Enhanced JPS (Java Process Status)
Lists all running JVM processes with their main class and arguments.
- Successfully identified closure-compiler processes
- Output: `/analysis-results/jps_list.txt`, `/analysis-results/jps_details.txt`

### 2. hh - Heap Histogram
Displays class histogram of the target JVM (similar to `jmap -histo`).
- Ran against closure-compiler process (PID with JMX on port 9010)
- Total instances: ~642,656-851,226 objects
- Total heap: ~20-58 MB
- Top classes by memory:
  1. com.google.javascript.rhino.Node$StringNode (~68K instances, ~3.8MB)
  2. com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.StandardUnionFind$Node (~133K instances, ~4.3MB)
  3. com.google.javascript.rhino.Node (~45K instances, ~2.5MB)
  4. com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.EqualityChecker (~92K instances, ~3MB)
  5. com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.parser.util.SourcePosition (~142K instances, ~4.6MB)
- Output: `/analysis-results/hh_output.txt`, `/analysis-results/hh_output2.txt`, `/analysis-results/hh_output3.txt`, `/analysis-results/hh_final.txt`

### 3. gc - GC Tracker
Prints GC log-like information for remote process.
- Successfully captured G1 GC events including:
  - G1 Young Generation collections
  - G1 Concurrent GC events
  - Memory allocation rates and GC intervals
  - Metaspace growth: 15MB -> 27MB
  - G1 Old Gen growth: 3MB -> 63MB
- Output: `/analysis-results/gc_output.txt`, `/analysis-results/gc_output2.txt`

### 4. mx - MBean Query
Queries MBean attributes from the target JVM via JMX.
- **Memory**: Heap usage (45MB used / 512MB max), Non-heap usage (29MB)
- **Threading**: 17 threads (16 daemon, 19 total started)
- **Runtime**: OpenJDK 21.0.11, JVM input arguments captured
- **ClassLoading**: 4,138 loaded classes, 4,435 total loaded, 0 unloaded
- **OperatingSystem**: 288 processors, CPU load metrics
- **Compilation**: 43,134ms total compilation time
- **GC**: G1 Young Generation collection count/time, G1 Old Generation
- Output: `/analysis-results/mx_memory_output.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_memory_heap.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_nonheap.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_threadcount.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_runtime.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_classloading.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_compilation.txt`, `/analysis-results/mx_threading.txt`

### 5. vminfo - VM Info
Dumps JVM flags and system properties from local VM.
- Successfully captured 592 lines of JVM flag data
- Includes all HotSpot JVM configuration flags (GC, compiler, memory, etc.)
- Note: Perf counter access had compatibility issues with JDK 21 (module access)
- Output: `/analysis-results/vminfo_output.txt`

### 6. mxdump - MBean Dump
Dumps all MBean data as JSON.
- 779 lines of JSON output including:
  - Runtime info (VM name, version, classpath, system properties)
  - Memory pools and GC statistics
  - Threading statistics
  - Class loading data
- Output: `/analysis-results/mxdump_output.txt`

### 7. jcmd - JMX Command
Executes jcmd-like diagnostic commands via JMX.
- **Thread.print**: Full thread dump showing 42-50 threads including:
  - Main thread running CommandLineRunner -> AbstractCommandLineRunner -> Compiler
  - C2/C1 compiler threads
  - G1 GC threads (12 GC threads, 20 G1 Conc threads)
  - Reference handler, Finalizer, Signal Dispatcher, Service Thread
- **GC.class_histogram**: Complete class histogram with 1,916 class types, 684,587 total instances, 30.8MB
- **GC.heap_info**: G1 heap info (524MB total, 92MB used, 1MB regions)
- **VM.version**: OpenJDK 21.0.11+10-1-24.04.2-Ubuntu
- Output: `/analysis-results/jcmd_threadprint.txt`, `/analysis-results/jcmd_threadprint2.txt`, `/analysis-results/jcmd_class_histogram.txt`, `/analysis-results/jcmd_heapinfo.txt`, `/analysis-results/jcmd_vmversion.txt`

### 8. mxping - JMX Connection Verification
Verifies JMX connectivity to the target JVM.
- Successfully connected via plain socket (non-TLS)
- Output: `/analysis-results/mxping_output.txt`

## Key Findings

### Memory Usage
- The closure-compiler uses approximately 45-63MB of heap during compilation
- 512MB max heap was configured
- Metaspace usage: 15-27MB (class metadata)
- Non-heap memory: ~29MB
- 4,138 classes loaded at runtime

### Thread Architecture
- Main thread delegates to compiler thread via CompilerExecutor
- Thread count peaks at 50 (including daemon threads)
- Uses G1 garbage collector with 12 GC threads and 20 concurrent marking threads
- Multiple C1/C2 JIT compiler threads for hot code optimization

### Object Distribution (Top memory consumers)
1. **Node$StringNode** - AST string nodes (~68K instances)
2. **StandardUnionFind$Node** - Union-Find data structure for type analysis
3. **Node** - AST nodes (~45K instances)
4. **EqualityChecker** - Type equality checking objects
5. **SourcePosition** - Source code position tracking
6. **Property$StringKey** - Property name keys
7. **TypedVar** - Typed variable references
8. **JSDocInfo** - JSDoc annotation information
9. **FunctionType** - JavaScript function type representations
10. **Property** - Object property representations

### GC Behavior
- G1 Young Generation collections occur every 200-700ms during compilation
- Allocation rate: 40-60 MB/s during active compilation
- GC pause times: 14-40ms for young generation
- No old generation (full) GCs observed during analysis

### Source Code Analysis
- 817 Java source files
- 274,880 total lines of code
- Largest files:
  1. NodeUtil.java (5,803 lines)
  2. Compiler.java (4,552 lines)
  3. IRFactory.java (4,352 lines)
  4. Node.java (3,938 lines)
  5. CompilerOptions.java (3,856 lines)
- Main packages: com.google.javascript.jscomp (1,377 classes), com.google.javascript.rhino (82 classes)
- 6,668 total classes in compiled JAR (including shaded dependencies)

## Environment
- Container: Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker)
- JDK: OpenJDK 21.0.11 (for running closure-compiler), OpenJDK 17 (for building jvm-tools)
- Maven: 3.8.7
- SJK: 0.24-SNAPSHOT (built from source)
- Closure Compiler: v20260629 (from Maven Central)

## Files Generated
All analysis results are saved in `/analysis-results/`:
- jps_*.txt - Process listing output
- hh_*.txt - Heap histogram outputs
- gc_*.txt - GC tracking outputs
- mx_*.txt - MBean query outputs
- vminfo_output.txt - VM flags and properties
- mxdump_output.txt - Full MBean JSON dump
- jcmd_*.txt - jcmd diagnostic command outputs
- mxping_output.txt - JMX connection verification
- source_stats.txt - Source code statistics
- jar_analysis.txt - JAR file analysis
- ANALYSIS_SUMMARY.md - This summary
SUMMARY
